author: NatureBlueee
text:
Claude Code added a command to count unfinished tasks. All 12 tests passed. An independent verifier reversed the condition to count finished tasks instead. All 12 still passed.

The test had created two tasks and completed one. The finished and unfinished counts both equaled one.

The verifier asked for an asymmetric case: three tasks, one completed, two unfinished. After that change, the same mutation made a test fail.

That small example came from testing an independent acceptance setup for Claude Code. It captures a problem we've also encountered in larger agent-written changes: an implementation and its tests can share the same blind spot.

One verifier reported five deliberately broken changes that left all 1,621 relevant tests green.

author: wmertens
text: @mattpocockuk A nice trick is e.g. to use a precommit hook to require an agent to run tests before committing. Sometimes it might forget but not if it gets the message at commit time

author: DYoung_AI
text: Concrete default: no merge of agent patches until upstream is green AND patch tests pass on the rebased tip. Two conditions, both on the same commit.
quoted:
feels like there needs to be a new way to distribute opensource software such that people can modify via agents but also get upstream automatically merged in

coding agents can do this but they won’t do it automatically
